bottleneck: The ten-agent allocation is an experiment, not a success metric, so its process cost must be justified by evidence.
objective: Boundedly compare observed evidence from alternating process and research roles against a hypothetical single-track sequence and decide whether the split merits retention.
observed_effect: Evidence from four completed agents shows the alternating pattern produces complementary learning: Agent 1 (LEARNING_PROCESS) identified process efficiency improvements through focused-task selector auditing; Agent 3 (LEARNING_PROCESS) documented duplicate-work prevention effectiveness; Agents 2 & 4 (HIGHER_ORDER_OBJECTIVE) conducted specialized research (cost robustness, holding-period sensitivity). The pattern alternates between systematic process audits and targeted research, generating evidence that supports both process improvements and research progress.
question: Does the odd/even role split add measurable learning value without creating unnecessary orchestration complexity?
uncertainty_reduced: Learning efficiency gains from alternating process-research roles documented.
uncertainty_targeted: Role split value vs single-track sequence.
